question.text: A 1-day VaR of Rs. 1 cr at 95% scales to a 10-day VaR approximately by:

explanation.text: The Logic: Standard assumption: returns are IID, so σ scales as √t. 10-day VaR = 1-day VaR × √10 ≈ Rs. 3.16 cr. The Trap: Linear scaling is the naive error; no scaling is wrong. Cross-Exam Context: IV covers square-root-of-time; XXI-B builds. Manager's Pro-Tip: Square-root-of-time scaling assumes constant volatility and no autocorrelation — breaks during crisis periods.
